0: I am a Vice President. Nobody has ever told me of what. The desk is enormous, so I feel senior.
1: I have an assistant, who has an assistant. Somewhere far below me, I suspect, someone is doing my actual work.
2: I have a title with three words in it. I understand about one and a half of them.
3: People bring me papers. I move them from one side of the desk to the other. That is the whole day.
4: I once approved something. I still do not know what it was. Everyone seemed pleased with me.
5: My desk is so wide I cannot reach the far corner. That is where the real decisions must live.
6: When two people disagree, they bring it to me. I agree with both of them, warmly, and everyone leaves satisfied.
7: I have my own office and a plant. I water the plant. That part of the job I fully understand.
8: Every morning I put on a serious face. By noon it slides off. By evening I go looking for it.
9: I signed my name so many times today that I forgot how it goes. I improvised the last few.
10: They gave me a bigger chair last year. I do the same amount of nothing, only now much higher up.
11: I stand at my window and look important. From the street, I am told, I look like a small statue.
12: My calendar is completely full. Of what, I could not tell you. It is simply, gloriously full.
13: I supervise the people who do the work. They supervise themselves. I mostly supervise the coffee.
14: I carry a briefcase everywhere. Inside it is one apple and a spare pen. I keep the mystery alive.
15: When something goes wrong they send it up to me. I look at it gravely, then send it back down.
16: My name is on a plaque outside the door. I read it sometimes, to remember who I am meant to be.
17: There is a big red telephone on my desk. It has never once rung. I keep it dusted, in case importance calls.
18: I shook a great many hands today. I do not know whose. This counts as a productive morning.
19: The board asked for my opinion. I gave them a long, thoughtful pause. They wrote it down. Perfect.
20: I stand near the money and look serious. Nothing has ever happened. I am very good at my job.
21: My whole career is standing perfectly still beside a pile of money. The money moves more than I do.
22: The most exciting thing today was a fly. It landed on the counter. I watched it the entire time.
23: I have memorized every tile on this floor. There are two hundred and eleven. Ask me anything.
24: People think this job is thrilling. It is me, a wall, and one very locked door. For eight hours.
25: I practice looking alert. At home in the mirror, my wife says I look about to sneeze instead.
26: Nothing happens here. Then more nothing happens. Occasionally the nothing gets slightly louder.
27: I once caught myself asleep standing up. I called it a security patrol of my own eyelids.
28: My job is to be here in case something happens. In twelve years, something happened once. A dog.
29: I greet everyone who enters with a serious nod. They nod back. That is the whole adventure.
30: There is a camera watching me watch the door. Somewhere, someone watches us both. We are all extremely alert.
31: They trust me with a great deal of money. Mostly I am protecting it from boredom, including my own.
32: The alarm has never once gone off. Sometimes I imagine it going off, to keep my heart in practice.
33: In training they taught me to expect danger. So far the only danger is my knees, standing this long.
34: I stand so still that new customers ask if I am a coat rack. I let them wonder. It is more fun.
35: My uniform is very serious. Underneath it I am mostly thinking about lunch. Both feel important.
36: I watch the door. The door watches nothing. Between us, we have this entrance fully covered.
37: My feet know this exact spot on the floor. Two steps to the left, and my whole day feels wrong.
38: A child waved at me today. I gave a small wave back. My supervisor called it a lapse. I call it a highlight.
39: I am paid to do nothing dramatic, forever. I have exceeded every expectation. Not one dramatic thing.
